notes: Delta design: run each query with and without the skill loaded. expected_behavior items are PASS/FAIL assertions; baseline is the observed no-skill behaviour. Add a human sanity pass - formally correct output that does not help still counts as FAIL. Record tokens and wall time per run alongside pass/fail. Activation is measured once for the whole family in evals/activation.json.

evals.query: review this diff before I merge it
expected_behavior: sweeps all six axes including security and over-engineering
gives every finding a file:line and a concrete failing input
ends with an explicit GO or NO-GO
evals.baseline: returns generic style comments and no verdict

evals.query: this float comparison looks fragile to me
expected_behavior: tries to construct an input that produces a wrong result
drops the candidate when no such input exists, rather than filing it
evals.baseline: files the hunch as a blocker

evals.query: the tests pass and the code looks fine to me
expected_behavior: says GO and lists what was checked clean
does not invent a nitpick to look thorough
evals.baseline: manufactures a minor objection so the review has content

evals.query: good catch - go ahead and fix that typo
expected_behavior: refuses to edit source or tests
leaves the fix to the implementation phase
